newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Carpetright current sales up 4 pct.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Carpetright current sales up 4 pct.

text.p: British carpet and floorcoverings group Carpetright Plc said on Tuesday comparable store sales rose four percent in the seven weeks since the beginning of May.
Chairman and chief executive Lord Harris said the carpet market was recovering after slackening off sharply in early 1997.
In calendar 1996 the overall market was up by five percent, he said, but in the first four months of 1997 it dropped by 10 percent, which was surprising.
Carpetright had seen a four percent increase in like for like sales since the start of its current year. "We're feeling the recovery already," Harris told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Harris said the carpet market had slowed down sharply before the last three general elections, and this year's was no exception.
The group increased market share last year to about 17 percent from 13 and aims to take 30 percent of the market over time.

Harris said the recovery in the market in the past few weeks suggested carpets might benefit from some of the windfall cash flowing to consumers from the demutualisation of building societies such as Halifax and Alliance and Leicester .
"The last couple of weeks have been picking up, there's a bit of evidence," he said.

Capital expenditure last year was 32.5 million stg, up from 22 million in the previous year. This year Harris estimated capital spending would be lower at around 14 million stg, because of fewer opportunities to buy freehold sites.
The group said it would look for opportunities for buying further freeholds, which it would finance from cash flow.
Harris was confident about prospects for the group's new more upmarket Carpet Depot format, which could eventually have 120 "showroom-only" stores and 120 superstores across Britain.
In the current year Carpetright expects to open 39 stores, including 20 more Carpetright outlets.
Earlier Carpetright reported a 28 percent increase in pretax profits to 32.2 million stg for the year to end April 1997.
It's shares rose strongly on the results and its current sales performance and were 40.5 pence higher by 0810 GMT.
Harris's family hold a 20 percent stake in the company, which he founded nine years ago. In January he sold four million of his shares.
